```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
```

## The 7 Components of a ggplot2 Chart

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
 A *`ggplot2`*  graphic is assembled from up to 7 parts (often less):

1. **Data** — the foundation
2. **Mapping** — translate data to aesthetics
3. **Layers** — geometric representations
4. **Scales** — control axes and legends
5. **Facets** — small multiples
6. **Coordinates** — spatial interpretation
7. **Theme** — visual look & feel

<p style="font-size:0.6em; color:#93a1a1;">At minimum: **data**, a **mapping**, and one **layer**.</p>
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
![](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/articles/ggplot2_files/figure-html/overview_graphic-1.png){width=100%}
:::

::::

## 1. Data and `ggplot()`

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
ggplot2 works best with **tidy data** (Rows = observations; Columns = variables)

The first step is to pass the data to `ggplot()` 

```{r data, eval=FALSE}
ggplot(data = mpg)
```
or 

```{r datatidy, eval=FALSE}
mpg %>% 
  ggplot()
``` 

<p style="font-size:0.65em; color:#93a1a1;">This creates an empty canvas — no visual output yet, but the data is ready.</p>

:::

::: {.column width="45%"  .column-small}
```{r data-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.height=5}
ggplot(data = mpg) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5,
           label = "Empty canvas\n(data loaded,\nno layer yet)",
           size = 6, color = "#586e75",
           hjust = 0.5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

**The `mpg` dataset** used in all examples:

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `cty`, `hwy` | City / highway mpg |
| `class` | Type of car |
| `drv` | Drive train |
| `displ` | Engine displacement |


:::

::::

## 2. Mapping: The link between variables and graphic attributes

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
A mapping links **variables** into **graphics attributes** (or aesthetic), 
acting as a  dictionary between data and graphics.

```{r mapping, eval=FALSE}
mpg %>% 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = cty, y = hwy)
```

The `aes()` function pairs:

- **Aesthetic**:  `x`, `y`, `colour`, `fill`, with 
- **Variables**:  `cty`, `hwy`, `class` in `mpg` data set

<p style="font-size:0.65em; color:#93a1a1;">This creates a frame with axis, scales and labels. No data yet.</p>


:::

::: {.column width="45%" .column-small}
```{r mapping-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.height=5}
ggplot(mpg, mapping = aes(x = cty, y = hwy)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Axes defined, no geometry yet",
       x = "City mpg (cty)",
       y = "Highway mpg (hwy)") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10,
                                   color = "#586e75"))
```

Key aesthetic attributes:

| Aesthetic | Controls |
|-----------|----------|
| `x`, `y` | Position |
| `colour`, `fill` | Colour |
| `size`, `shape` | Point style |
| `alpha` | Transparency |

:::

::::

## 3. Layers: The heart of a ggplot2 chart

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
The most common layer is the **Geometry**  defining *how* data is displayed

```{r layers, eval=TRUE, fig.show='hide'}
mpg %>% 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = cty, y = hwy) +
  geom_point()              # scatterplot 
 
```

One can add layers: 

```{r layers2, eval=TRUE, fig.show='hide'}
mpg %>% 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = cty, y = hwy) +
  geom_point() +              # scatterplot 
  geom_smooth(formula = y ~ x,
              method = "lm")  # linear trend 
```

Two layers stacked with `+`:  
`geom_point()` + `geom_smooth()`
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

```{r layers-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.height=5}
ggplot(mpg, aes(cty, hwy)) +
  geom_point(color = "#2A9D8F", alpha = 0.7) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Scatterplot (basic)",
       x = "City mpg (cty)",
       y = "Highway mpg (hwy)") 
```


```{r layers-plot2 , echo=FALSE, fig.height=5}
ggplot(mpg, aes(cty, hwy)) +
  geom_point(color = "#2A9D8F", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(formula = y ~ x, method = "lm",
              color = "#E9C46A") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Scatterplot with linear regression",
       x = "City mpg (cty)",
       y = "Highway mpg (hwy)") 
```
:::

::::

## 4. Scales

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
Scales **translate**  what is shown on the graph back to an understanding of the data — axes, legends, colour,  bars.


```{r scales, eval=TRUE, fig.show='hide'}
mpg %>% 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = cty, y = hwy) +
  geom_point() +         
  scale_colour_viridis_d()
```

<p style="font-size:0.65em; color:#93a1a1;"> Formally, `scale` is a function from a region in the data space (the domain of the scale) to a region in aesthetic space (the range of the scale). </p>


:::

::: {.column width="45%" .column-small}
```{r scales-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.height=5}
ggplot(mpg, aes(cty, hwy, colour = class)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "City mpg", y = "Highway mpg",
       colour = "Class")
```

**Scales controls**:

- Axis limits and breaks
- Label formatting  
- Colour palettes
- Data transformations (`log`, `sqrt`...)

:::

::::

## 5. Facets: Graphics by groups 

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
Facets split the data into **small multiples** and separate panels for subsets of the data according to a factor variable.

```{r facets, eval=TRUE, fig.show='hide'}
mpg %>% 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = cty, y = hwy) +
  geom_point() +         
  facet_grid(~year)
```

Two facet functions:

- `facet_grid(row ~ col)` — strict grid
- `facet_wrap(~ var)` — wraps into space

<p style="font-size:0.65em; color:#93a1a1;">Here: 2 years =  2 panels or 2 years  x 3 drives = 6 panels</p>
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r facets-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.height=5}
ggplot(mpg, aes(cty, hwy)) +
  geom_point(color = "#2A9D8F", alpha = 0.6, size = 1.5) +
  facet_grid(~year ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "City mpg", y = "Highway mpg")
```
 or with `year~drv`
```{r facets-plot6, echo=FALSE, fig.height=5}
ggplot(mpg, aes(cty, hwy)) +
  geom_point(color = "#2A9D8F", alpha = 0.6, size = 1.5) +
  facet_grid(year~drv ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "City mpg", y = "Highway mpg")
```

:::

::::

## 6. Coordinates: Fix positions

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
Coordinates interpret **position aesthetics**. The default is Cartesian, but alternatives exist:


```{r coords, eval=TRUE, fig.show='hide'}
mpg %>% 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = cty, y = hwy) +
  geom_point() +         
  coord_fixed()
```

<p style="font-size:0.65em; color:#93a1a1;">Here: 1 unit on x = 1 unit on y, making slope visually meaningful.</p>
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r coords-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.height=5}
ggplot(mpg, aes(cty, hwy)) +
  geom_point(color = "#2A9D8F", alpha = 0.7) +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "City mpg", y = "Highway mpg",
       title = "Fixed aspect ratio")
```

| Function | Use |
|----------|-----|
| `coord_fixed()` | Equal x/y units |
| `coord_flip()` | Swap x and y |
| `coord_polar()` | Polar / pie charts |
| `coord_map()` | Map projections |


:::

::::

## 7. Theme: The look and feel

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}

The theme controls **all non-data visuals**: background, grid lines, fonts, legend position, axis styling.

```{r theme, eval=TRUE, fig.show='hide'}
mpg %>% 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = cty, y = hwy) +
  geom_point() +         
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    axis.line = element_line(
      linewidth = 0.75),
    axis.line.x.bottom = element_line(
      colour = "blue")
  )
```

Built-in themes: `theme_minimal()`, `theme_bw()`, `theme_classic()`, `theme_void()`...
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r theme-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.height=5}
ggplot(mpg, aes(cty, hwy, colour = class)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 0.75),
    axis.line.x.bottom = element_line(colour = "blue")
  ) +
  labs(x = "City mpg", y = "Highway mpg",
       colour = "Class")
```
:::

::::

## Putting it all together

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
All 7 components combined with `+`:

```{r combining, eval=TRUE, fig.show='hide'}
mpg %>% 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = cty, y = hwy) +
  geom_point( mapping = aes(colour = displ)) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c() +
  facet_grid(year ~ drv) +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor =
          element_blank())
```

Each `+` adds a new component.  
Order matters for **layers**; less so for others.
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r combining-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.height=5}
ggplot(mpg, aes(cty, hwy)) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(colour = displ), alpha = 0.8) +
#  geom_smooth(formula = y ~ x, method = "lm") +
  scale_colour_viridis_c() +
  facet_grid(year ~ drv) +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```
:::

::::

## Summary

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}

| Component | Function(s) | Required |
|-----------|-------------|----------|
| Data | `ggplot(data)` | Yes
| Mapping | `aes()` | Yes|
| Layers | `geom_*()`, `stat_*()` | Yes|
| Scales | `scale_*()` | — |
| Facets | `facet_grid/wrap()` | — |
| Coordinates | `coord_*()` | — |
| Theme | `theme_*()`, `theme()` | — |

**To learn more:**

- [ggplot2-book.org](https://ggplot2-book.org/) (free online)
- [ggplot2.tidyverse.org](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org)

:::

::: {.column width="45%" .column-small}

**The ggplot2 recipe:**

1. Start with `ggplot(data)`
2. Map variables with `aes()`
3. Add geometry with `geom_*()`
4. Refine with scales, facets, coordinates, and theme
5. Layer components with `+`


```{r summary-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.height=3.5}
ggplot(mpg, aes(cty, hwy, colour = class)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 7)) +
  labs(x = "City mpg", y = "Highway mpg",
       colour = NULL)
```

:::
